_comment: Raptor's egg library (library/README.md). Written for Raptor from linkding's documentation; no upstream egg.
name: linkding
author: support@raptorpanel.net
description: linkding is a minimal, fast bookmark manager with tags, search and browser extensions. The egg runs it with SQLite and makes the admin account from its settings; there are no sign-ups.
startup: cd app; want="$(sha256sum raptor-requirements.txt | cut -d' ' -f1) $(python3 --version)"; if [ "$want" != "$(cat ../venv/.raptor-installed 2>/dev/null)" ]; then echo "Installing linkding's packages"; rm -rf ../venv; python3 -m venv ../venv && ../venv/bin/pip install -q --no-cache-dir --disable-pip-version-check -r raptor-requirements.txt && echo "$want" > ../venv/.raptor-installed || { echo "Linkding's packages couldn't be installed. Restart to try again."; exit 1; }; fi; export PATH=/home/container/venv/bin:$PATH DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE=bookmarks.settings.prod; [ -n "$LD_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD" ] || unset LD_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD; if [ ! -f data/db.sqlite3 ] && [ -z "${LD_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD:-}" ]; then echo "Set Admin password first: without it, nobody could sign in."; exit 1; fi; python manage.py generate_secret_key && python manage.py migrate && python manage.py enable_wal && python manage.py create_initial_superuser && python manage.py migrate_tasks || exit 1; exec uwsgi --http 0.0.0.0:{{SERVER_PORT}} --ini raptor-uwsgi.ini

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# linkding: linkding publishes its releases only as a container image, so
# this takes the app (with its built web assets) out of the official image
# on Docker Hub, every layer checked against its SHA-256, and lists the
# exact Python packages that release was built with. They're installed into
# the server's venv folder on the next start, by the server's own Python.
# Your bookmarks (the data folder) are never touched.
set -euo pipefail
cd /mnt/server
work=/mnt/server/.raptor-build
rm -rf "$work" && mkdir -p "$work"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
fail() { echo "$1"; exit 1; }
ua="raptor-installer (+https://raptorpanel.net)"
get() { curl -fsS --retry 3 -A "$ua" "$@"; }

case "$(uname -m)" in
    x86_64) arch=amd64 ;;
    aarch64) arch=arm64 ;;
    *) fail "linkding has no build for this CPU ($(uname -m))." ;;
esac

# The release, from GitHub (gh-release says why when it doesn't exist); the
# image's tag is the version without the v.
version="${VERSION:-latest}"
[ "$version" = latest ] || version="v${version#v}"
tag=$(gh-release tag sissbruecker/linkding "$version") || exit 1
v=${tag#v}

if [ -f app/manage.py ] && [ "$(cat .linkding-version 2>/dev/null)" = "$v" ]; then
    echo "linkding $v is already installed."
else
    echo "Downloading linkding $v"
    repo=sissbruecker/linkding
    reg=https://registry-1.docker.io/v2/$repo
    token=$(get "https://auth.docker.io/token?service=registry.docker.io&scope=repository:$repo:pull" | jq -r .token) ||
        fail "Docker Hub can't be reached right now. Reinstall to try again."
    auth="Authorization: Bearer $token"
    index=$(get -H "$auth" -H "Accept: application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json, application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.list.v2+json" "$reg/manifests/$v") ||
        fail "linkding's image for $v isn't on Docker Hub. Set Version to latest, or to another release, then reinstall."
    digest=$(jq -r --arg a "$arch" 'first(.manifests[] | select(.platform.os == "linux" and .platform.architecture == $a) | .digest) // empty' <<<"$index")
    [ -n "$digest" ] || fail "linkding $v has no image for this CPU ($arch)."
    layers=$(get -H "$auth" -H "Accept: application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json, application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.v2+json" "$reg/manifests/$digest" | jq -r '.layers[].digest') ||
        fail "Docker Hub can't be reached right now. Reinstall to try again."
    mkdir -p "$work/root"
    for layer in $layers; do
        get -L -H "$auth" -o "$work/layer" "$reg/blobs/$layer" || fail "The download failed. Reinstall to try again."
        [ "sha256:$(sha256sum "$work/layer" | cut -d' ' -f1)" = "$layer" ] || fail "The download didn't match its checksum. Reinstall to try again."
        # Only the app's folder: the rest is the image's operating system.
        tar -xf "$work/layer" -C "$work/root" --no-same-owner --wildcards 'etc/linkding/*' 2>/dev/null || true
        rm -f "$work/layer"
    done
    app="$work/root/etc/linkding"
    [ -f "$app/manage.py" ] && [ -d "$app/static" ] && [ -d "$app/.venv" ] || fail "linkding's image didn't have the files it should. Reinstall to try again."
    # The packages the image was built with, at the same versions. Its
    # programs are built for a newer Debian, so the server builds its own
    # venv; uWSGI comes as pyuwsgi, the same server packaged as a wheel
    # (published a little after uWSGI itself, so the newest 2.0).
    find "$app/.venv/lib" -maxdepth 3 -name '*.dist-info' -printf '%f\n' | sed 's/\.dist-info$//' |
        awk '{ i = index($0, "-"); n = substr($0, 1, i - 1); ver = substr($0, i + 1); gsub("_", "-", n); n = tolower(n)
               if (n == "uwsgi") print "pyuwsgi>=2.0.30,<2.1"; else if (n != "psycopg-c" && n != "supervisor") print n "==" ver }' |
        sort > "$app/raptor-requirements.txt"
    grep -q '^django==' "$app/raptor-requirements.txt" || fail "linkding's image didn't list its packages. Reinstall to try again."
    # Its SQLite search extension is built for that newer Debian too.
    rm -rf "$app/.venv" "$app/data" "$app/libicu.so"
    rm -rf app.old
    [ ! -d app ] || mv app app.old
    mv "$app" app
    rm -rf app.old
    echo "$v" > .linkding-version
fi
# uWSGI's settings: the image's, without its root-only parts (switching
# user, the stats port), with the background tasks (favicons, previews,
# archiving) run by uWSGI itself. The port comes from the startup.
cat > app/raptor-uwsgi.ini <<'INI'
[uwsgi]
module = bookmarks.wsgi:application
env = DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE=bookmarks.settings.prod
route = ^/static/ addheader:Content-Security-Policy: sandbox
static-map = /static=static
static-map = /static=data/favicons
static-map = /static=data/previews
static-map = /robots.txt=static/robots.txt
processes = 2
threads = 2
buffer-size = 8192
vacuum = true
die-on-term = true
master = true
if-not-env = LD_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS
attach-daemon2 = cmd=python manage.py run_huey -f,stopsignal=15
endif =
INI
# Bookmarks live next to the app, so a new version never touches them.
mkdir -p data/favicons data/previews data/assets
ln -sfn ../data app/data
echo "Installed linkding $v."

variables.name: Version
variables.description: The linkding version to install, such as 1.47.0, or latest. Reinstall to change it.

variables.name: Admin username
variables.description: The admin account made on the first start.

variables.name: Admin password
variables.description: The admin account's password, used when the account is made. Change it in linkding's settings afterwards.
